stem: The Sun, the planets, their moons and other bodies orbiting the Sun together form the __________.
solution: The solar system consists of the Sun and everything bound to it by gravity — planets, moons, asteroids and comets.

stem: The number of planets in our solar system is __________.
solution: There are eight planets in the solar system since Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

stem: The planet nearest to the Sun is __________.
solution: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.

stem: The largest planet in the solar system is __________.
solution: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system.

stem: The planet known as the 'Red Planet' is __________.
solution: Mars appears reddish due to iron oxide (rust) on its surface, so it is called the Red Planet.

stem: The planet famous for its prominent rings is __________.
solution: Saturn is best known for its spectacular system of rings.

stem: The only planet known to support life is __________.
solution: Earth is the only planet known to support life, thanks to water, a suitable atmosphere and temperature.

stem: The natural satellite of the Earth is the __________.
solution: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite.

stem: The Sun is a __________.
solution: The Sun is a star — a huge, hot ball of glowing gases at the centre of our solar system.

stem: Planets do not have their own light; they are seen because they __________.
solution: Planets shine by reflecting sunlight; unlike stars, they do not produce their own light.

stem: The rotation of the Earth on its axis causes __________.
solution: The Earth's spin (rotation) on its axis causes the cycle of day and night.

stem: The Earth takes about __________ to complete one rotation on its axis.
solution: The Earth completes one rotation in about 24 hours, giving one day.

stem: The Earth takes about __________ to complete one revolution around the Sun.
solution: One revolution of the Earth around the Sun takes about 365¼ days — one year.

stem: The revolution of the Earth around the Sun, along with the tilt of its axis, causes __________.
solution: The Earth's revolution combined with its axial tilt causes the changing seasons.

stem: The changing appearance of the Moon over a month is called the __________.
solution: As the Moon orbits Earth, the lit portion we see changes — these are the phases of the Moon.

stem: A full moon and a new moon are examples of the Moon's __________.
solution: Full moon and new moon are two of the Moon's phases seen during its monthly cycle.

stem: A group of stars forming a recognisable pattern in the sky is called a __________.
solution: A constellation is a pattern of stars, such as Orion or the Great Bear (Saptarshi/Ursa Major).

stem: The star that appears almost fixed in the northern sky and helps in finding directions is the __________.
solution: The Pole Star (Dhruva) lies nearly above the Earth's north pole and appears fixed, aiding navigation.

stem: The constellation Ursa Major is also popularly known as the __________.
solution: Ursa Major, the Great Bear, is called Saptarshi in Indian tradition and helps locate the Pole Star.

stem: Small rocky bodies that orbit the Sun mostly between Mars and Jupiter are called __________.
solution: Asteroids are small rocky bodies, most orbiting in a belt between Mars and Jupiter.

stem: A celestial body with a bright head and a long glowing tail, seen occasionally, is a __________.
solution: A comet is made of ice and dust and develops a glowing tail as it nears the Sun.

stem: A streak of light seen in the night sky when a small body burns up in the atmosphere is a __________.
solution: A meteor, or 'shooting star', is the bright streak from a small body burning as it enters the atmosphere.

stem: A meteor that survives its fall and lands on the Earth's surface is called a __________.
solution: A meteorite is the remnant of a meteor that reaches the Earth's surface.

stem: A huge system of billions of stars, gas and dust held together by gravity is a __________.
solution: A galaxy is an enormous collection of stars, gas and dust bound by gravity.

stem: Our solar system is part of the galaxy called the __________.
solution: The Sun and its planets lie in the Milky Way galaxy, called Akash Ganga in Indian tradition.

stem: Objects that revolve around a planet are called its __________.
solution: Satellites (moons) are bodies that orbit a planet, like Earth's Moon.

stem: The correct order of the first four planets from the Sun is __________.
solution: From the Sun outward, the first four planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.

stem: The four planets nearest the Sun (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars) are called __________ planets.
solution: The inner four planets are rocky (terrestrial) planets with solid surfaces.

stem: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune are called __________ because they are large and made mostly of gases.
solution: The outer four planets are gas giants, large planets composed mainly of gases.

stem: Pluto is now classified as a __________.
solution: In 2006 Pluto was reclassified from a planet to a dwarf planet.

stem: Which planet is called Earth's 'twin' because of its similar size?
solution: Venus is often called Earth's twin because it is close to Earth in size, though very different in conditions.

stem: The force that keeps the planets moving around the Sun is __________.
options: the gravitational pull of the Sun
solution: The Sun's gravity holds the planets in their orbits.

stem: The Moon has no light of its own; a full moon shines because __________.
options: it reflects sunlight towards the Earth
solution: The Moon reflects sunlight; during a full moon, the sunlit face is turned fully towards Earth.

stem: The surface of the Moon has many bowl-shaped depressions called __________.
solution: The Moon's surface is covered with craters formed by impacts of meteorites.

stem: There is no air or life on the Moon because the Moon __________.
options: has almost no atmosphere and no liquid water
is too far from any star
solution: The Moon lacks a significant atmosphere and liquid water, so it cannot support life as we know it.

stem: The apparent movement of stars across the night sky is mainly due to __________.
solution: Stars appear to move across the sky because the Earth rotates on its axis.

stem: India's space research organisation, which launches satellites and missions, is __________.
solution: ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation) carries out India's space missions and satellite launches.

stem: An artificial satellite is __________.
options: a man-made object placed in orbit around the Earth for uses like communication
solution: Artificial satellites are human-made objects orbiting Earth, used for communication, weather, navigation and research.

stem: Which of the following is a use of artificial satellites?
solution: Artificial satellites are used for communication, weather forecasting, navigation, television and more.

stem: The tail of a comet always points __________ the Sun.
solution: A comet's tail points away from the Sun because it is pushed by the solar wind and radiation.

stem: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a star from a planet?
options: A star produces its own light; a planet reflects light
A planet produces its own light; a star reflects light
solution: Stars generate their own light through nuclear reactions; planets merely reflect starlight.

stem: The blinking or twinkling of stars is due to __________.
options: the bending of their light as it passes through the Earth's atmosphere
solution: Starlight is refracted and disturbed by the moving atmosphere, making stars appear to twinkle.

stem: Which body is at the centre of the solar system?
solution: The Sun lies at the centre of the solar system, with planets orbiting it.

stem: The first human to travel into space was __________.
solution: Yuri Gagarin of the Soviet Union was the first human to travel into space, in 1961.

stem: The first person to walk on the Moon was __________.
solution: Neil Armstrong was the first human to set foot on the Moon, in 1969.

stem: The first Indian to travel to space was __________.
solution: Rakesh Sharma became the first Indian in space in 1984.

stem: Ancient people used the positions of stars and the Sun mainly to __________.
options: find directions and keep track of time and seasons
solution: Observing celestial bodies helped ancient people navigate, track time and mark seasons for farming.

stem: A solar eclipse occurs when the __________ comes between the Sun and the Earth.
solution: In a solar eclipse, the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth, casting its shadow on Earth.

stem: A lunar eclipse occurs when the __________ comes between the Sun and the Moon.
solution: In a lunar eclipse, the Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon, casting its shadow on the Moon.

stem: India's Moon mission that made a soft landing near the lunar south pole in 2023 was __________.
solution: Chandrayaan-3 achieved a soft landing near the Moon's south pole in 2023.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Beyond Earth' is that:
options: Earth is part of a vast solar system and universe of stars, planets and other bodies that we study through observation and space science
Earth is the only object in space
stars and planets are the same
solution: The chapter introduces the solar system and universe — the Sun, planets, moons, stars and other bodies — and how we study them.

stem: The Sun, the planets, their moons, and other objects held together by the Sun's gravity form the:
solution: The Solar System consists of the Sun and all the objects that revolve around it — the planets, their moons, asteroids, comets and meteoroids — held together by the Sun's gravity.

stem: The star at the centre of our Solar System is the:
solution: The Sun, a star, is at the centre of our Solar System; it provides light and heat and its gravity holds the planets in their orbits.

stem: How many planets are there in our Solar System?
solution: There are eight planets in our Solar System — Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. (Pluto is now classified as a dwarf planet.)

stem: The planet closest to the Sun is:
solution: Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun; it is also the smallest planet in the Solar System.

stem: The largest planet in the Solar System is:
solution: Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System; it is a giant gas planet with a famous 'Great Red Spot' and many moons.

stem: The planet known for its beautiful rings is:
solution: Saturn is famous for its bright, beautiful rings made of ice and rock particles; it is the second-largest planet.

stem: The only planet known to support life is:
solution: Earth is the only planet known to support life, because it has the right conditions — water, oxygen, a suitable temperature and a protective atmosphere.

stem: The planet called the 'Red Planet' because of its reddish appearance is:
solution: Mars is called the 'Red Planet' because of the reddish colour of its surface, caused by iron oxide (rust) in its soil.

stem: The natural satellite of the Earth is the:
solution: The Moon is the Earth's only natural satellite; it revolves around the Earth and reflects the Sun's light.

stem: The Moon does not produce its own light; it shines because it:
options: Reflects the light of the Sun
solution: The Moon has no light of its own; it appears bright because it reflects the sunlight falling on it.

stem: The different shapes of the bright part of the Moon seen from Earth over a month are called the:
solution: The phases of the Moon are the different shapes of the illuminated (bright) part of the Moon seen from Earth (like new moon, crescent, half and full moon) as it revolves around the Earth.

stem: A huge system of billions of stars, gas and dust held together by gravity is called a:
solution: A galaxy is a vast system of billions of stars, along with gas and dust, held together by gravity; our Solar System is part of a galaxy called the Milky Way.

stem: The galaxy in which our Solar System is located is the:
solution: Our Solar System is located in the Milky Way galaxy, which contains hundreds of billions of stars.

stem: Everything that exists — all galaxies, stars, planets and space — is together called the:
solution: The Universe is everything that exists — all matter, energy, galaxies, stars, planets and the space between them; it is vast beyond imagination.

stem: Small rocky bodies that revolve around the Sun, mostly between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter, are called:
solution: Asteroids are small rocky bodies that revolve around the Sun, most of them found in the 'asteroid belt' between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.

stem: A celestial body with a bright head and a long tail that revolves around the Sun in a long path is a:
solution: A comet is a body made of ice, dust and gas that revolves around the Sun; when it comes near the Sun, it develops a glowing head and a long, bright tail.

stem: A 'shooting star' streaking across the night sky is actually a:
options: Meteor (a meteoroid burning up in the atmosphere)
solution: A 'shooting star' is a meteor — a small piece of rock (meteoroid) from space that burns up due to friction as it enters the Earth's atmosphere, producing a streak of light.

stem: A meteoroid that does not burn up completely and lands on the Earth's surface is called a:
solution: A meteorite is a meteoroid that survives its passage through the atmosphere and lands on the Earth's surface.

stem: Stars appear to twinkle in the night sky, whereas planets:
options: Generally do not twinkle (they shine steadily)
solution: Stars appear to twinkle because their light is bent by the moving air of the atmosphere, while planets, being closer, generally shine with a steadier light and do not twinkle much.

stem: A group of stars forming a recognisable pattern in the sky is called a:
solution: A constellation is a group of stars that appear to form a recognisable pattern or shape in the sky, such as Ursa Major (the Great Bear / Saptarishi) and Orion.

stem: The star that appears almost fixed in the northern sky and helps in finding directions is the:
solution: The Pole Star (Polaris) appears almost stationary in the northern sky (above the North Pole) and has long been used by travellers and sailors to find the north direction.

stem: The Earth rotates on its axis, which causes:
solution: The Earth's rotation on its axis (once about every 24 hours) causes day and night, as different parts of the Earth face the Sun at different times.

stem: The Earth's revolution around the Sun (once a year) is responsible for the:
solution: The Earth's revolution around the Sun, together with the tilt of its axis, causes the seasons over the course of a year.

stem: Artificial satellites are man-made objects placed in orbit around the Earth to:
options: Help in communication, weather forecasting, navigation and observation
solution: Artificial satellites are man-made objects launched into orbit around the Earth; they help in communication (TV, phones), weather forecasting, navigation (GPS), and Earth and space observation.

stem: India's space agency, which launches satellites and space missions, is:
solution: ISRO (the Indian Space Research Organisation) is India's national space agency; it launches satellites and space missions like Chandrayaan (to the Moon) and Mangalyaan (to Mars).

stem: India's Moon missions are named:
solution: India's Moon (lunar) missions are named Chandrayaan; Chandrayaan-3 successfully landed near the Moon's south pole in 2023. Mangalyaan was India's Mars mission.

stem: Which statement about the Solar System is correct? (i) The Sun is at the centre (ii) There are eight planets (iii) Earth is the only planet with life
solution: All three are correct: the Sun is at the centre of the Solar System, there are eight planets, and Earth is the only planet known to support life.

stem: A telescope is an instrument used to:
options: Observe distant objects in the sky (stars, planets, galaxies)
solution: A telescope is an instrument that makes distant objects in the sky (like stars, planets, moons and galaxies) appear larger and clearer, helping astronomers study them.

stem: The correct order of the first four planets from the Sun is:
solution: The first four planets from the Sun, in order, are Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars — the inner (rocky) planets.

stem: Pluto is now classified as a:
solution: Pluto, once considered the ninth planet, is now classified as a dwarf planet, because it does not meet all the criteria to be called a full planet.

stem: The planets that are made mostly of gases (the gas giants) include Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and:
solution: The gas giants — Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune — are the large outer planets made mostly of gases; the inner four (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars) are rocky planets.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches an object with its description? (i) Sun – a star (ii) Moon – Earth's satellite (iii) Jupiter – largest planet
solution: All three are correctly matched: the Sun is a star, the Moon is Earth's natural satellite, and Jupiter is the largest planet.

stem: The vast distances in space are measured in units like the:
options: Light year (the distance light travels in one year)
solution: Because distances in space are enormous, they are measured in units like the light year — the distance light travels in one year (about 9.46 trillion kilometres).

stem: The overall importance of studying space and the Solar System is that it helps us:
options: Understand our place in the universe and develop technologies (satellites, weather, navigation)
solution: Studying space helps us understand our place in the universe, learn about the Earth and other worlds, and develop useful technologies like satellites for communication, weather forecasting and navigation.

stem: The astronaut who was the first human to travel into space was:
solution: Yuri Gagarin, a Soviet cosmonaut, became the first human to travel into space in 1961, orbiting the Earth aboard the spacecraft Vostok 1.

stem: The first Indian to travel into space was:
solution: Rakesh Sharma became the first Indian to travel into space in 1984, aboard a Soviet spacecraft; famously, when asked how India looked from space, he replied 'Saare Jahan Se Achha'.
